title: Rice/Paddy — Pest Management: BPH, Stem Borer, Gall Midge
content:
MAJOR INSECT PESTS OF PADDY:

1. BROWN PLANT HOPPER (BPH) — Nilaparvata lugens:
Symptoms: Circular drying patches (hopperburn), honeydew, sooty mold.
Management: BPMC 50 EC @ 1.5 L/ha. Thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 100 g/ha. Buprofezin 25 SC @ 1 L/ha.
DRAIN FIELD WATER before spraying — directs spray to base of plants.
BPH RESISTANCE: Avoid prophylactic insecticide use. Use resistant varieties.

2. YELLOW STEM BORER (Scirpophaga incertulas):
Symptoms: Dead heart (vegetative) or White ear head (reproductive).
Management: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (Coragen) @ 150 ml/ha at 20 and 40 DAT.
Cartap hydrochloride 50 SP @ 1 kg/ha.
Trichogramma japonicum egg cards @ 5 cards/ha at heading.

3. GALL MIDGE (Orseolia oryzae):
Symptoms: Elongated silver shoot — tubular leaf, no grain set.
Management: Carbofuran 3G @ 25 kg/ha at 10-15 DAT. Chlorpyriphos 20 EC @ 1.5 L/ha.
Use resistant varieties: Jyothi, BPT-5204 are moderately resistant.

4. LEAF FOLDER (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis):
Symptoms: Leaves folded and stitched, white streaks on leaves.
Management: Chlorpyriphos 20 EC @ 1.5 L/ha. Indoxacarb 14.5 SC @ 500 ml/ha.

5. WHORL MAGGOT:
Symptoms: Wilting of central shoot in early stage.
Management: Usually self-limiting. If severe: Phorate 10G @ 10 kg/ha.

IPM FOR RICE:
- Light traps @ 1/ha for stem borer/leaf folder moths.
- Pheromone traps @ 5/ha for yellow stem borer.
- Release of Trichogramma japonicum 1.5 lakh eggs/ha at egg masses.
- Do not apply synthetic pyrethroids — kills BPH natural enemies, causes resurgence.
